 Ty Jerome amassed 31 points (8-of-17 FGs, 14-of-14 FTs), four rebounds, six assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Sunday’s win over the Kings.
 For those who believed Jerome would cool off after scoring 73 points in the Grizzlies’ first two games, that didn’t happen on Sunday. He did most of his damage inside the arc, making 7 of 11 two-point attempts and shooting 14-for-14 from the foul line. Add in the assists, and it was another excellent night for those rostering Jerome, one of the best players in fantasy basketball so far. The Grizzlies play three games in Week 2, starting with the Jazz on Monday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Ty Jerome (back) is out for Saturday’s game against the Kings. 
 Jerome will miss a game for the first time this season. His absence likely means Cam Spencer will start, especially with Scotty Pippen Jr. (back) also out. Spence is worth streaming due to the absences. 
 Ty Jerome 
 MEM 
 Guard-Forward 
 #2 
 Ty Jerome (upper back) and Scotty Pippen Jr. (lower back) are questionable to play against the Kings on Saturday. 
 Ty Jerome has been one of the biggest surprises this season and has been a major steal for where people drafted him in redraft leagues. If he were to miss time, Scotty Pippen would be the guy to add in redraft leagues. If Pippen also misses time, then look at Cam Spencer to be the add. 
 Ty Jerome 
 MEM 
 Guard-Forward 
 #2 
 Ty Jerome struggled on Thursday and finished with just 10 points (3-of-12 FGs), two rebounds, three assists, two steals and one three-pointer against the Trail Blazers. 
 Less than an hour before tipoff, it was reported that Jerome was questionable for this game with back tightness. Despite the flare up, he was able to start, though it ended up being his worst performance of the season, and he only played 24 minutes. This is worth keeping an eye on, especially ahead of their next game against the Kings on Saturday. Cam Spencer and Scotty Pippen Jr. would fill out the point guard minutes if Jerome were unavailable. 
 Ty Jerome 
 MEM 
 Guard-Forward 
 #2 
 Ty Jerome struggled on Monday but still contributed 15 points (4-of-15 FGs), one rebound, eight assists, one steal and one three-pointer against the Jazz. 
 After a scorching start to the season, Jerome fell back to earth in this game. His shot simply didn’t fall at the same rate, though he made up for it by dishing out a season high for assists. Jerome has been unreal to start the season, but it was never likely that he would maintain that pace. However, he should be a fantastic fantasy option for the rest of the season and one of the best value picks in fantasy basketball. 
 Ty Jerome 
 MEM 
 Guard-Forward 
 #2 
 Ty Jerome accounted for 28 points (11-of-22 FGs, 3-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, five assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Warriors. 
 After scoring 45 points in Wednesday’s opener, Jerome appeared to be coming down to earth in the first half of Friday’s game. However, after scoring eight first-half points on 3-of-7 shooting, the Grizzlies point guard put up 14 points in the third quarter. Jerome and the Grizzlies ripped off a 17-0 run in the fourth to move to 2-0 on the season, getting their four-game road trip off to a good start. 
 Ty Jerome 
 MEM 
 Guard-Forward 
 #2 
 Ty Jerome leads the charge with 45 points (17-of-25 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), six rebounds, five assists, a block, and five 3-pointers in win against the Jazz. 
 Ty Jerome led this team in shot attempts and was very efficient. The Jazz had no way to stop him, and he was the reason that this game got out of hand so early in the second quarter. He got into the paint whenever he wanted and took advantage of Jaren Jackson being in foul trouble. While he likely won’t continue to lead the team in shot attempts, he could be in line for a big year that could result in him having a top 50 fantasy season. 
 Ty Jerome 
 MEM 
 Guard-Forward 
 #2 
 Ty Jerome had 17 points (6-of-13 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, three steals and three three-pointers in Friday’s exhibition against the Hornets. 
 Jerome has remained the starting point guard this preseason. While the Grizzlies should continue to play a deep rotation this year, Jerome averaged 19.7 points, 5.7 assists and 2.8 threes in 15 games last year while he only averaged 22.7 minutes. He should pay of his eighth-round cost in fantasy drafts without a significant minutes increase and would be a steal with additional minutes. 
 Ty Jerome 
 MEM 
 Guard-Forward 
 #2 
 Ty Jerome had 16 points (5-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), one rebound, four assists and four three-pointers in the Grizzlies’ preseason win over the Bulls on Friday. 
 Jerome was excellent as the 29-year-old point guard gets ready for the regular season. In just 14 minutes, he had 16 points, four assists and four three-pointers. Jerome played only 15 games for Memphis last year, but averaged 19.7 points, 5.7 assists and 2.8 threes. He’s coming off the board in the eighth-round of fantasy drafts this year. 
 Ty Jerome 
 MEM 
 Guard-Forward 
 #2 
 Ty Jerome accumulated 12 points (4-of-8 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), five assists and one block over 15 minutes in Monday’s preseason win over the Hawks. 
 It’s notable that Jerome got the start over Scotty Pippen Jr. during Memphis’ preseason opener and he responded by pouring in 10 first-half points on 4-of-8 shooting as Memphis exploded for 82 points in an impressive opening half. It’s fair to wonder whether Jerome can build off his initial success with the Grizzlies last year when he averaged 19.7 points while shooting over 42 percent from three-point range after finally making his season debut in late January.

 Cam Spencer (back) and Ty Jerome (ankle) are out for Friday’s game against the Jazz. 
 The Grizzlies will once again be without Spencer and Jerome, which limits their perimeter depth. Javon Small and Walter Clayton Jr. are questionable; they’ll be handling the playmaking responsibilities on Friday if available.
